title: A map the model draws itself
allegory: A latent space is a map the model draws for itself: a clerk writes down each picture's address, a painter paints whatever lives at an address, and the map is only useful if nearby addresses paint similar pictures and there are no blank streets in between.
map: a latent vector z: the bottleneck's coordinates
the clerk who writes down addresses
the painter who paints what lives at an address
walking the straight street from the 2s to the 7s
interpolating between two latent vectors and decoding each point
claiming a fuzzy neighbourhood instead of one house
a VAE encoding each input as a cloud with centre μ and width σ

cap.1: An autoencoder squeezes each picture into a few numbers and rebuilds it. But feed it a random set of numbers and it paints mush. Why?
cap.2: A plain autoencoder reconstructs well, yet its latent space is irregular: neighbouring points can decode very differently and much of the space decodes to nothing. So you can't sample new images from it.
cap.3: Reconstruction loss never regularises the latent geometry, so the encoder's image is an arbitrary, gappy subset, and a straight line between two encodings need not decode to anything plausible.

cap.1: Think of the numbers as an address on a map the model draws itself. A clerk writes down each picture's address; a painter paints whatever lives at an address.
cap.2: The encoder maps each input to a point z in a small space; the decoder maps z back to an image. That small space is the latent space: the coordinates the bottleneck learned.
cap.3: The latent space is the encoder's output space, far lower-dimensional than the input. Training on reconstruction alone learns a code that inverts well, not a geometry that means anything.

cap.1: Walk the straight street from the 2's address to the 7's. On a good map every house along the way paints something that looks like a digit.
cap.2: Interpolate: z(t) = (1−t)·z₂ + t·z₇ for t from 0 to 1, and decode each point. On a well-shaped latent space the images shade from a 2 to a 7 through plausible in-betweens.
cap.3: Interpolation is the standard probe of latent geometry. In a VAE the path between the 2 and 7 clusters decodes to digits ambiguous between the two; in a plain autoencoder it can cross junk.

chapters.name: Fuzzy neighbourhoods

right.title: VAE
lines: each picture claims a fuzzy patch

chapters.verdict: Give every picture a cloud, not a point, and the map fills in.

cap.1: The fix: let each picture claim a small fuzzy neighbourhood, not one house. The painter must work from anywhere in it, so the map fills in and neighbours agree.
cap.2: A VAE's encoder outputs a centre μ and a width σ, and z is sampled from that cloud. Rebuilding from anywhere in the cloud pushes different images apart and fills the gaps between them.
cap.3: Encode x as N(μ, σ²), sample z = μ + σ·ε so gradients reach μ and σ (the reparameterisation trick), and add a KL pull toward N(0, I). Kingma and Welling, ICLR 2014.

cap.1: A sneaky failure: every address paints the same blurry digit. The painter learned to work alone, and the map stopped meaning anything.
cap.2: Posterior collapse: the KL term drops to zero, the encoder outputs μ ≈ 0 and σ ≈ 1 for every input, and z carries no information. Print mean σ each epoch; it should sit below 1.
cap.3: A decoder strong enough to reconstruct without z lets the encoder match the prior everywhere. Monitor KL per latent dimension, and ramp the KL weight up from 0 (KL warm-up).

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Walk between two points to test a map
Every model keeps a private map

cap.1: Every model you study keeps its own private map. Asking what lives near here, and what lies between, is how you start reading it.
cap.2: GAN latents, the residual stream and SAE latents are all learned coordinate spaces. Interpolating, clustering and hunting for meaningful directions are the same moves you make here.
cap.3: Interpretability and steering treat activation space as a latent space: find directions that mean something, then move along them. This week's grid of decoded digits is that idea in miniature.

coda.title: Tap to place pictures on the map, then compare houses with fuzzy neighbourhoods

readouts.label: map covered as 3×3 fuzzy patches
readouts.f: round(100*sum(G.map((row, r) => sum(row.map((v, c) => G.some((row2, r2) => row2.some((v2, c2) => v2 && abs(r - r2) <= 1 && abs(c - c2) <= 1)) ? 1 : 0))))/64) + '%'

readouts.label: squares claimed by 2+ pictures (where in-betweens live)
readouts.f: sum(G.map((row, r) => sum(row.map((v, c) => sum(G.map((row2, r2) => sum(row2.map((v2, c2) => (v2 && abs(r - r2) <= 1 && abs(c - c2) <= 1) ? 1 : 0)))) >= 2 ? 1 : 0))))

caption.1: Tap squares to place pictures. As single houses they cover almost none of the map; as fuzzy 3×3 patches they cover most. Place two close and watch them share.
caption.2: A random address only paints something real if it lands on claimed ground. Points leave the map nearly blank; clouds fill it, and where two clouds overlap you get the in-between digits.
caption.3: A caricature of why σ > 0 plus a KL pull toward the prior makes the latent samplable: coverage rises from n/64 to near 1, and overlaps are where interpolations blend.

where_else: GANs also generate from a latent, reached by a completely different route
The residual stream: interpretability reads activations as a space with meaningful directions
Sparse autoencoders learn a dictionary of latents for a model's activations
The reparameterisation trick recurs wherever a model has to sample and still be differentiable

hamming.what: The small coordinate space an encoder maps inputs into, where position is supposed to mean something.
hamming.when: Whenever a model compresses inputs through a bottleneck and you want to sample from it, interpolate in it or read what it learned.
hamming.why: A latent space is only useful if nearby points mean similar things and the gaps decode sensibly, which a plain autoencoder never guarantees and a VAE forces.

object.title: The fuzzy-neighbourhood map
object.subtitle: Height is how likely an address is to paint a real digit. Widen the clouds and the islands join.

cap.1: A plain autoencoder's map: needles where training digits landed, flat ground everywhere else. Most addresses paint mush.
cap.2: With σ near zero each input is a single point. Almost all of the latent space decodes to nothing plausible.
cap.3: A deterministic encoder occupies a measure-zero set of the latent; the prior's mass lands mostly off it.

cap.1: From above: the 2s and the 7s are islands, and the street between them crosses empty ground.
cap.2: Interpolating from the 2 cluster to the 7 cluster passes through regions no input was ever encoded to.
cap.3: Linear paths between encodings leave the support of the encoded data, so decodes along them are unconstrained.

cap.1: Give each picture a fuzzy neighbourhood and the needles grow into hills. The street from 2 to 7 now stays on higher ground.
cap.2: A VAE samples z from a cloud around each encoding, so the decoder learns to paint from a whole region, not a point.
cap.3: Sampling z ~ N(μ, σ²) during training forces the decoder to be smooth over each posterior's support.

cap.1: Halfway between 2 and 7, a good map paints a digit that could be either. That is where in-betweens live.
cap.2: Where neighbouring clouds overlap, decodes blend: the midpoint of 2 and 7 looks ambiguous between them.
cap.3: Overlapping posteriors make the decoder interpolate between classes, which is what makes latent traversals meaningful.

cap.1: Wide clouds merge into one plateau: almost any address paints a digit, so you can sample new ones. Push to the limit and every cloud is the same cloud.
cap.2: The KL term pulls σ towards 1, reconstruction pulls it towards 0; mean σ should settle below 1. At the extreme you get posterior collapse.
cap.3: If every posterior equals the prior, KL is zero and z carries no information: coverage without meaning.

predict.q: You decode a random point from a plain autoencoder's latent space. What do you usually get?

options.t: Mush: most of the space decodes to nothing

predict.why: Nothing asks a plain autoencoder to fill its map, so random addresses usually land on blank ground.

predict.q: Why does encoding each input as a cloud, not a point, help?

options.t: The decoder must work from anywhere in the cloud, so the map fills in
It makes the network smaller and faster

predict.why: Clouds from different images must stay apart to be decodable, and together they cover the space.

predict.q: In VAE training the KL term falls to zero and every sample looks the same. What happened?

options.t: Posterior collapse: z carries no information

predict.why: The encoder matched the prior everywhere and the decoder worked alone. Watch mean σ; it should sit below 1.

object.where: Any learned space you sample from or walk through: GAN latents, the residual stream, SAE dictionaries.
